Overview
IMA Tech (the “Company,”
“we,” “us” or “our”) was incorporated under the laws of the State of Wyoming on March 29, 2023. Our
fiscal year ends on April 30.
From inception through the
fiscal year ended April 30, 2026, our business was the development and deployment of digital avatars — software combining artificial
intelligence with niche databases to deliver interactive, personalized consultation and instructional content through a website at https://ima.gg,
which we launched on April 1, 2024. During the fiscal year ended April 30, 2026, and in connection with the change in control described
below, our management determined to abandon that business. The digital avatar business has been discontinued, and the results of that
business are presented as a discontinued operation in the financial statements included in this report.
Shell Company Status
We are a shell company as
that term is defined in Rule 405 under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and Rule 12b-2 under
the Exchange Act, meaning a registrant with no or nominal operations and with assets consisting solely of cash and cash equivalents, or
assets consisting of any amount of cash and cash equivalents and nominal other assets. Our shell status has the following consequences,
among others:
·
Rule 144 is not available . Under Rule 144(i), securities issued by a current or former shell
company may not be resold in reliance on Rule 144 unless and until the issuer has ceased to be a shell company, has filed Form 10 information
reflecting its status as an entity that is not a shell company, is subject to the reporting requirements of Section 13 or 15(d) of the
Exchange Act and has filed all required reports for the preceding twelve months, and at least one year has elapsed since the filing of
that Form 10 information.
·
The safe harbor for forward-looking statements is unavailable . The safe harbor provided
by Section 27A of the Securities Act and Section 21E of the Exchange Act does not apply to statements made by a blank check company or
an issuer of penny stock.
·
Form S-8 is unavailable . A shell company may not use a registration statement on Form S-8,
and may not do so until sixty calendar days after it has filed Form 10 information reflecting that it is no longer a shell company.
·
Form 10 information will be required upon an acquisition . If we complete a transaction that
causes us to cease to be a shell company, we will be required to file a Current Report on Form 8-K containing the information that would
be required in a registration statement on Form 10, within four business days of completion of the transaction, pursuant to Item 2.01(f)
of Form 8-K.
Corporate History and Recent Developments
Change in Control —
December 31, 2025 . Effective December 31, 2025, a change in control of the Company occurred. Pursuant to a stock purchase agreement,
Wang Hui acquired 1,500,000 shares of our common stock, representing approximately 57.47% of our then-outstanding common stock, from Liliia
Havrykh, our founder and then sole executive officer. The total consideration paid by Mr. Wang was $441,036.60 in cash, paid at the closing.
The Company received no part of that consideration. In conjunction with the transaction, Ms. Havrykh resigned as President, Chief Executive
Officer, Treasurer, Secretary and a director, Daniel Jozef Szaruga resigned as a director, Mateusz Jakubowki resigned as a director, and
Mr. Wang was appointed as our sole director, President, Chief Executive Officer, Treasurer and Secretary.
Amended and Restated
Articles of Incorporation . On January 20, 2026, Wang Hui, as the holder of a majority of our voting power, acted by written consent
to approve the adoption and filing of Amended and Restated Articles of Incorporation with the Secretary of State of the State of Wyoming,
to be filed not earlier than March 17, 2026, following dissemination of an Information Statement on Schedule 14C. We intend to file such
Amended and Restated Articles of Incorporation in the near future.
Letter of Intent —
Shenzhen Jingbao . On January 29, 2026, we entered into a non-binding Letter of Intent to acquire Shenzhen Jingbao Supply Chain
Technology Co., Ltd. (“Shenzhen Jingbao”), an international logistics company headquartered in Shenzhen, China, with branches
in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Quanzhou, Xiamen, Yiwu and Qingdao. Shenzhen Jingbao was owned by Wang Hui, who was at that time our sole officer
and director, and the Letter of Intent was therefore a related-party arrangement. The Letter of Intent contemplated that we would issue
a combination of common stock and Series A Preferred Stock as consideration, and that a definitive agreement would be completed on or
about February 15, 2026, following completion of administrative actions required under applicable law of the People’s Republic of
China.
No definitive agreement was
executed, and the proposed acquisition was not completed. Following the change in control described below, we are not pursuing the acquisition
of Shenzhen Jingbao.
Change in Independent
Registered Public Accounting Firm . On March 2, 2026, Mac Accounting Group & CPAs, LLP resigned as our independent registered
public accounting firm, and on the same date our Board of Directors appointed Boladale Lawal & Co. as our independent registered public
accounting firm. See Item 9. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure .
Change in Control —
June 17, 2026 . Effective June 17, 2026, after the end of the fiscal year covered by this report, a second change in control occurred.
Pursuant to a stock purchase agreement, Inderjit Mangat acquired the same 1,500,000 shares of our common stock, representing approximately
57.47% of our outstanding common stock, from Wang Hui. The total consideration was $300,000, consisting of $75,000 in cash and a secured
promissory note in the principal amount of $225,000, payable $112,500 on July 15, 2026, and $112,500 on August 15, 2026, delivered at
the closing. As security for that note, the shares are pledged in favor of Mr. Wang. The Company received no part of the consideration
and is not a party to the note or the pledge. In conjunction with the transaction, Mr. Wang resigned as our sole director, President,
Chief Executive Officer, Treasurer and Secretary, and Ms. Mangat was appointed to each of those offices.
In connection with that transaction
our principal executive offices were relocated from Shanghai, China to 11336 Franklin Boulevard, Elk Grove, California 95757.
Expansion of the Board
of Directors . On July 31, 2026, our Board of Directors expanded the size of the Board from one to two members in accordance with
our Bylaws, and appointed Lucky Lakhwindar Janda as a director, effective immediately, to fill the resulting vacancy.
Plan of Business
Acquisition
Objective . Our objective is to acquire interests in income-producing real property that we believe can generate current cash flow
and appreciate in value over a long-term holding period. We expect to pursue acquisitions of individual properties and of portfolios,
and we may also acquire an operating company whose principal assets are real property interests. We have not adopted, and our board of
directors is not required to adopt, any policy limiting the percentage of our assets that may be invested in any single property, in any
single asset class or in any single geographic market.
Target
Property Criteria . In evaluating a prospective acquisition we expect to consider, among other factors, the following. No single
factor will be controlling, and we may acquire a property that does not satisfy all or any of these criteria.
·
Asset type . Our management will consider any type of real estate investment opportunity.
·
Geography . While management intends to focus of properties located in California, it will consider
properties outside this area of focus.
·
Transaction size . Individual acquisitions with a purchase price of up to $10 million, subject to
the availability of financing.
·
Occupancy and lease profile . The credit quality of in-place tenants, the weighted average remaining
lease term, rent relative to prevailing market rents, the allocation of operating expenses, capital expenditure and real estate tax obligations
between landlord and tenant, as well as the presence of renewal, expansion, termination or purchase options.
·
Physical condition . The age, construction type and condition of improvements, deferred maintenance,
the remaining useful life of major building systems and anticipated capital expenditures.
·
Cash flow . In-place and projected net operating income, the capitalization rate implied by the
purchase price and projected cash-on-cash return after debt service.
·
Financing . The availability, cost and terms of mortgage financing, including whether existing financing
may be assumed, and any prepayment restriction, lockout or defeasance obligation.
